before.title: Beluga whale · revised adult exterior and face
before.author: 3D Assets (CC0 source); PhenoVoxel Archive (MIT additions)
before.delivery: Bundled original CC0 GLB retained byte-exact. Active control surface is extensively resampled/resculpted with new appendages, face, oral anatomy and original skin maps.
before.biology: Contributor-reported AI-generated static model. Source dimensions are asset authoring units, not biological measurements; no source skeleton, animation or tissue data. New selected adult exterior is reference-led and unvalidated.
changes: Retained the untouched CC0 starting file. Added denser anterior control stations to the resculpted surface, a rounded cap and a fuller, distinct melon/short rostrum/neck profile. Removed the former zero-at-pole axial bump that folded nose rings back through one another.

Rebuilt pectorals as swept solid cambered foils with full roots and thinner trailing edges. Revised the fluke leading/trailing contours. New layered small eyes and tapered skin eyelids replace dot-like eyes and tube lids; lip overlays removed in favour of a continuous shallow skin groove.

New original cream-grey skin, fine normal and variable roughness fields with sparse authored pale marks. Appendages use body-position UV coordinates so facial tones do not appear on flippers. Reduced beluga fill/rim lighting leaves the surface volume visible.

Existing bounded posterior stroke, glide, neck, turning, melon and separate feeding/oral actions retained and checked against the revised geometry. Selected36peg teeth remain an authored anatomy display. No measured individual, living scan, tissue mechanics, pressure/prey/water solver or scientifically validated motion.
Recessed and curved the oral floor, palate and tongue, adding restrained original vertex colour variation and posterior depth tones. The internal display remains simplified and unvalidated.

viewerRig.description: Dorsoventral heave and fluke pitch guided by Fish (1998) beluga cohort; slow exterior feeding sequence with separate oral-display action. Selected spatial masks, body bends and timing remain uncalibrated.

after.title: Beluga whale · long full adult, rounded melon and detailed ivory skin
after.author: 3D Assets (CC0 source); PhenoVoxel Archive (MIT additions)
after.delivery: Original CC0 reference GLB retained byte-exact. The active continuous exterior, swept appendages, face, skin and finite surface articulation are independently authored.
after.biology: Contributor-reported AI-generated static model. Source dimensions are asset authoring units, not biological measurements; no source skeleton, animation or tissue data. New selected adult exterior is reference-led and unvalidated.
changes: Selected body frame lengthened from 4.50 to 5.15 through the trunk, retaining a compact head. The central trunk is eight percent fuller with two actual concave ventrolateral folds. Normalized display proportions are not measurements extracted from photographs.

Adaptively refined continuous anterior mesh, compact rounded melon, short projecting muzzle, soft chin, smaller dark recessed eyes, tapered almond-shaped eyelids and softened neck creases. The original CC0 starting reference remains separate and unchanged.

Original generated ivory pigment and model-guided material paintings mapped to separate head and trunk charts. Registered fine epidermal normals and roughness, actual-triangle local ambient occlusion and wet dielectric highlights improve surface depth. No supplied-photo pixels are redistributed.

Seven finite swimming, glide, flexible-neck, turning, melon, pursed-feeding and oral-display studies retain the same 3D surface. Vertical posterior stroke and selected fluke pitch use the retained Fish (1998) cohort context; the studies are authored and uncalibrated.

viewerRig.description: Dorsoventral heave and fluke pitch guided by Fish (1998) beluga cohort; slow exterior feeding sequence with separate oral-display action. Selected spatial masks, body bends and timing remain uncalibrated.

viewerRig.spatialScale: Selected5.15-unit longitudinal frame with a fuller trunk and fixed-size head, built from a4.50-unit construction frame. Normalized display, not measured dimensions extracted from the supplied mixed photographs.
viewerRig.surface: Independent continuous exterior with locally refined face, separate spherical head and cylindrical trunk material charts, and separate swept appendages. Original CC0 source remains a retained reference.

before.status: Revised after user rejection of the previous cartoon-like appearance; actual viewer comparisons and software checks recorded with remaining limits
remaining: Selected adult phenotype and normalized scale; the mixed still photos cannot establish one individual, sex, stock, body condition, exact dimensions or continuous timing.
The face, shoulder junction, oral tissues, blubber folds and authored skin remain reconstructions. No scan, fitted skeleton/muscles, tissue-volume model or complete internal anatomy.
Anchored finite stroke and feeding studies do not solve swimming trajectory, thrust, buoyancy, pressure, prey/water transport, swallowing, breathing or acoustic function.

Available local browser renders use software compatibility lighting. WebGL optical appearance and photorealism have not been established; the previous version was rejected by the user as cartoon-like.

Observed limits: simplified oral tissues and circular pursing contour, visible shoulder/ridge joins, and tiny raster lip marks. These changes improve the authored model but do not establish a photorealistic animal.

before.description: Revised adult beluga exterior with a rounded melon, short projecting rostrum, shallow mouth groove, fuller chin, small recessed layered eyes and tapered skin eyelids. Swept pectorals have thick roots, curved leading edges and thinner trailing edges; revised flukes remain horizontal and notched. Original cream-grey skin has restrained irregular pigmentation, fine relief and sparse pale marks. The original CC0 AI-origin starting file is retained; this authored derivative is not a living scan or a measured animal. Finite swimming, neck, melon and feeding studies remain illustrative and unvalidated.
